interest: Japanese army strains: Korean volunteers, morale and a mutiny.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.22 covers personnel, organization, discipline, mutiny, and military service in the Japanese armed forces between February 1938 and July 1939. Comprising military and naval attaché intelligence reports, diplomatic telegrams, and cross-reference sheets, the file documents key personnel policies and command developments during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Prominent subjects include the drafting of imperial regulations establishing a limited voluntary enlistment system for Koreans in the Japanese Army and American analysis of colonial attitudes; high-level command reassignments in China, notably General Shunroku Hata replacing General Iwane Matsui and General Hajime Sugiyama succeeding General Hisaichi Terauchi amid political maneuvering; and disciplinary crises in the field, including an armed mutiny of Japanese troops at Tangku refusing deployment to Shanxi, reported Italian casualties in downed Japanese aircraft over Lanzhou, and widespread discontent among Japanese troops in Central China.

subfiles.about: Military attaché intelligence report concerning the Japanese War Office plan to establish a voluntary military service system for Koreans in the Imperial Japanese Army.
subfiles.from: Captain John Weckerling, Assistant Military Attaché, Tokyo (approved by Major Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché)
subfiles.summary: Military Attaché report on Korean army volunteers from 1938, seen as a symbolic gesture.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 919 on Korean Volunteer Service in the Japanese Army
subfiles.to: War Department / Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording a Navy Department telegram reporting the replacement of General Iwane Matsui by General Shunroku Hata in China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: General Matsui replaced by General Hata, 1938.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Relief of General Matsui by General Hata

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Peiping telegram 695 regarding rumors and reasons concerning the replacement of General Terauchi by General Sugiyama in North China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: General Terauchi replaced by General Sugiyama in North China, 1938.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Replacement of General Terauchi by General Sugiyama

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting that General Terauchi has been recalled and replaced by General Sugiyama as commander of Japanese forces in North China due to political friction.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart reports General Terauchi recalled and Sugiyama in command, blamed on Doihara's maneuvering.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 695 from Lockhart (Peiping) on Command Shakeup in North China

subfiles.about: Naval attaché report detailing an armed mutiny of Japanese troops at Tangku who refused deployment to Shanxi after expecting repatriation to Japan.
subfiles.from: Commander Harvey E. Overesch, U.S. Navy, Naval Attaché, Peiping
subfiles.summary: Commander Overesch reports a mutiny by about 200 Japanese troops at Tangku in 1939, put down with two NCOs killed.
subfiles.title: Naval Attaché Report No. 12 on Mutiny of Japanese Troops at Tangku
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Chungking telegram 255 reporting that Italian bodies were allegedly discovered in Japanese aircraft downed over Lanzhou.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Italians reportedly found in downed Japanese planes at Lanchow.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Aerial Combat over Lanchow and Italian Casualties

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording reports from Hankow regarding widespread discontent and morale issues among Japanese troops in Central China.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Discontent Among Japanese Troops in Central China
